rows.medi_said: أنا أملوهن هلأ. أنا أمل-- أملهم هلأ.
rows.why: Asked عملتهم؟ he answered with a broken past form (amalhon / amalhom) for 'I did them'; she recast عملتهم and he said Yes.
'Let's see if I did them right' needs iza (if), not inno/inha; she asked 'إنه or إذا?' pointing at the wrong linker.
rows.english: For now let's see if I did them right.

rows.medi_said: ست أيام أسبوع ولا أسبوع؟ (I don't know how to say per.)
rows.why: He said he did not know how to say 'per' and left أسبوع bare; Amal supplied بالاسبوع (her line is stamped 06:10, out of order in the transcript).

rows.medi_said: لا، بشتغل بس. أنا ن-نمت أكثر
rows.why: She asked about today in the past (ما اشتغلت؟); he answered in the present بشتغل where the past اشتغلت fits; she let it pass.
rows.english: No, I did work, but I slept more.

rows.medi_said: أنا أخذت وقت إضافه لـ قهوة
rows.amal_said: وقت زيادة يمن؟ ... إضافة ... it's فصحى. We say زيادة in spoken.
rows.why: He used MSA إضافة for 'extra'; Amal recast وقت زيادة and said إضافة is Fusha, spoken is زيادة (sheet: extra / increase | Ziaadeh | زيادة).
rows.english: I took extra time for coffee.

rows.why: Describing what he is wearing today he said bare البس (no b-); بلبس (or the participle لابس, B15) fits; she let it pass.

rows.amal_said: No. What's the other way to say it? ... أول مرة إلي ... The عندي rule is just with مفضل.
rows.why: For 'my first time' he used عندي; Amal said No and taught أول مرة إلي - عندي only goes with مفضل (Latin in transcript).

rows.medi_said: El mara el awwal andi? / So el mara el awwal eli wouldn't make sense.
rows.why: مرة is feminine so the adjective after it is el-oola; Amal recast المرة الأولى and he said 'El mara el ula ... You didn't correct me on the other one'.

rows.medi_said: el mara el thani, yeah, is also second time / marra thani means another time
rows.why: مرة is feminine, so after it the adjective is el-tanye / tanye; he said el thani / thani twice and Amal discussed the meaning but let the form pass.

rows.medi_said: so aglab el marra is most of the time.
rows.amal_said: Yeah, but we don't say that. So أغلب الوقت.
rows.why: 'Most of the time' is أغلب الوقت; مرة is an occurrence, Amal said 'we don't say that' and gave الوقت.

rows.amal_said: No. ... Or maybe the it is feminine.
rows.why: 'The beginning of it' is awal + pronoun ending (awalo/awalha); he put min; Amal said No and he got to awala/awalaha.

rows.amal_said: No, kees is a plastic bag. ... Remember suitcase. ... Shanta.
rows.why: For 'bag' he tried كيس (plastic bag) then جزدان; Amal said No, kees is a plastic bag, and led him to شنتة (sheet: bag | Shanta | شنتة).

rows.amal_said: Does that sound right? ... Akhir shantata means like the end of her bag. ... That's the end of her bag.
rows.why: 'Her last bag' with آخر + el- / possessive means 'the end of (her) bag'; Amal prompted twice and he reached شنتة الـ أخيرة (Great job).
He put آخر after the noun with a pronoun ending; after the noun the adjective form a5eera is needed; Amal said No.

rows.amal_said: No. ... Just one way to say this thing.
rows.why: 'The end of our program' is آخر + noun with the pronoun ending (آخر برنامجنا), no el- and no لنا; Amal said No.

rows.amal_said: That's her last program. No. How do you say the end of?
rows.why: He used the adjective (and a plural أخرين) after the noun, which means 'her last program', not 'the end of'; Amal said No and he got آخر برنامجها.
'Our' program needs -na, he said -ha (her); Amal recast برنامجنا and he repeated it.

rows.amal_said: No. ... It means the beginning of their cat.
rows.why: 'Their first cat' with أول + a possessed noun means 'the beginning of their cat'; Amal said No (engine wrote بسيطًا for bsset-hom).
He put -na (our) on cat; Amal said 'Their.' to fix the owner ending (engine wrote بسطنا).

rows.medi_said: It's a olin? ... Is this plural?
rows.amal_said: لش. ... No, it's, it's not plural. ... Their first cat.
rows.why: He reached for the plural awwalin after a single feminine noun; Amal said it is not plural and he got ola.
The 'other way' for 'her second cup' is taani before the noun + إلها; he put the possessed noun first then ثانية لها; Amal said No, then Great for ثانية كاسا لها.
أسئلة is feminine so it grows -t before the owner ending (as2iltak); he dropped the t, Amal prompted and he said أسيليتك.
He guessed a plural Ajwab for 'answers'; Amal gave the plural أجوبة.

rows.amal_said: No. ... It's tied to غير. ... عن، عن.
rows.why: 'Other than / different from' is غير عن; he used min; Amal said No and gave عن (she says he keeps forgetting it).
He put a pronoun ending on عن and then a noun after it; after Amal's 'then everyone' he said 'ghayr ann ikul' and she said Yes.

rows.amal_said: Or that's like, um, unique maybe.
rows.why: Asked for another way to say 'another student' he said طالب مختلف (a different student); Amal pushed back ('that's like unique'); the drilled forms are طالب تاني / غير طالب.

rows.medi_said: This will be راح يكون الـأخر-- ... أخر مرة
rows.amal_said: Only one correction is مرة، مرة is feminine or masculine. So راح شو؟
rows.why: مرة is feminine so the verb is تكون; Amal named the gender of مرة and he said راح تكون.
rows.english: It will be the last time.

rows.why: A plain present verb needs b-; he said أملها, Amal recast بعملها and repeated it.
rows.english: The last time I do it.

rows.amal_said: You are bad. ... You don't need منكون، خلص، بس سيئين.
rows.why: No 'to be' in the plain present; Amal said 'You don't need منكون'.

rows.amal_said: You don't need منكون، خلص، بس سيئين.
rows.why: 'We two' needs the plural adjective سيئين; he said singular سيء; Amal recast سيئين and he repeated it.
'Bad at choosing' reads better as a noun after bi (بالاختيار); she let the verb بنختار pass.
عند takes ma, not mish; Amal said ما عنا twice.

rows.medi_said: Can I say تنين now both of us?
rows.why: He had used bare تنين for 'both of us' and then asked; Amal supplied إحنا الاثنين.
ra7 takes a bare verb; Amal repeated راح as a prompt, then said ندفع and he said 'إحنا راح نطفا كتير' (engine wrote بنفتح / بنطفأ for bnedfa3).
rows.english: But we're going to pay a lot.

rows.medi_said: و إذا بنـ-- إذا بنـ-- نطفا كتير بدنا إشي ممتاز و special.
rows.why: iza keeps the b- (إذا بندفع); he started بنـ twice then dropped it to نطفا and she did not fix the verb.
rows.english: If we pay a lot we want something excellent and special.

rows.amal_said: What's special? You know it. ... مميز.
rows.why: English 'special' in an Arabic sentence; on her sheet: special | Mumayyaz | مميز; Amal asked for it and supplied مميز.
rows.english: We want something excellent and special.

rows.medi_said: راح نكون متأخرين ... متأخرين أول طيارة.
rows.why: متأخر takes على; he left it out; Amal recast متأخرين على أول طيارة and he echoed 'متأخرين على؟'.
rows.english: We'll be late for the first flight.

rows.why: 'I kept using a lot of Arabic words' needs the plural كلمات; she laughed and let it pass.
rows.english: (I kept using) Arabic words a lot.

rows.medi_said: would it be اسباني إلي or اسباني أني؟
rows.amal_said: لا، I say إسباني، إسباني تبعي.
rows.why: He asked how to say 'my Spanish'; Amal supplied إسباني تبعي.

rows.medi_said: الـ قريب إن، قريب الـ... Last week. قريب آخر...
rows.amal_said: شو غريب آخر؟ ... You could say آخر، or you could say the past month. ... الشهر الماضي.
rows.why: He tried قريب (near) for 'last (week/month)'; Amal asked what he meant and gave آخر / الشهر الماضي.
Month is شهر (sheet: month | shahar | شهر); he said شهرة twice and Amal recast شهر.

rows.medi_said: قبل شهر، uh, ما، ما استعملت اسباني كتير.
rows.amal_said: Do, do you wanna say the last month؟ ... قبل is for ago.
rows.why: قبل + number = ago; for 'last month' it is الشهر الماضي; Amal asked if he meant 'the last month' and explained قبل is for ago.
rows.english: Last month I didn't use Spanish much.

rows.medi_said: So، شهر الماضي ما استعملت اسباني كتير.
rows.why: Right after her الشهر الماضي he dropped the first el-; noun + adjective needs el- on both; she let it pass.
rows.english: Last month I didn't use Spanish much.
